items.item_text: Master of Social Work (MSW) degree from an accredited institution and current California Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
Experience developing and facilitating educational programs, workshops, curricula, or training materials
Preferred: Experience working with parents/caregivers and community-based organizations.
Experience in childhood trauma, child sexual abuse, or related prevention programming

The UCLA Health Rape Treatment Center provides specialized services for child and adult victims of sexual assault and abuse and conducts prevention, education, and professional training designed to reduce sexual violence and strengthen community response. Prevention programming includes education for youth and other community audiences, training and consultation for schools and partner organizations, and collaboration with community and professional systems.

Come join our outreach team as a Parent/Caregiver Program Coordinator and make a difference in the community. This key role will develop, coordinate, and deliver sexual abuse prevention education to parents and caregivers.
Identifying opportunities to reach parent/caregiver audiences through community organizations, healthcare, schools and child-serving settings, and other community-based venues
Assesses prevention-education needs and develops programming responsive to those needs.

Creating and adapting prevention curricula and materials, facilitating workshops and trainings, developing community partnerships, evaluating program effectiveness, and contributing to ongoing program improvement.
Uses trauma informed approaches to respond appropriately to disclosures, connect families with clinical advocacy and community resources and supports caregiver engagement services.
Contributes to grant reporting and data requirements.

Regularly travels to local schools, community organizations, partner agencies, and other program sites throughout Los Angeles County; occasionally travel outside the local area may be required for training, meetings, or other program-related activities.
Participation in the RTC/Stuart House 24-hour on-call response system, including approximately 1-2 weekday overnight on-call shifts per month.
2+ years providing education, support, outreach or programming primarily to parent/caregivers or families
Live Scan Fingerprint screening, Criminal Record, Sex Offender Registry, and Child Abuse Index Clearance

Per funding agency requirements and alliances, all staff must complete background checks at least every five years that includes, sex offender registry check, State or FBI criminal history check, including fingerprint check, child abuse and neglect state registry check if available in the state of California.

Bilingual English/Spanish proficiency sufficient to deliver prevention programming and communicate effectively with participants (ability to successfully complete the UCLA language proficiency assessment)
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with parents/caregivers, schools, community organizations, healthcare providers, and multidisciplinary partners.
Strong written communication, organizational, project-management, and documentation skills.
Ability to work independently in community and off-site settings while managing multiple concurrent activities and deadlines.
